prompt: A school picture-day portrait from around 2003, the kind of glossy print that came home in a cardboard folder with a sheet of wallet-sized copies. A figure in a plain black knitted balaclava sits upright on a low photographer's stool, shoulders turned slightly to one side the way pupils were always angled, chin a touch down, eyes looking dead into the lens with calm, polite stillness. Only the eyes show through the two eye holes; the knit is completely plain and unmarked. Black woollen gloves rest one over the other on its knee, and it wears a tidy navy V-neck school jumper over a white collared shirt, collar slightly crooked. Behind it hangs the familiar mottled canvas backdrop, cloudy grey-blue darkening toward the edges, softly out of focus. The light is flat and forgiving: a big soft main light from front-left and a gentle fill, so the mask and eyes are evenly lit with a small catchlight in each eye and almost no shadow, plus a faint hair light rimming the top of the head. Head-and-shoulders crop, centred, medium telephoto compression, camera at chest height. The colour is that slightly too-smooth, warm-skewed minilab print of the era: lifted blacks, creamy highlights, a gentle magenta-blue cast, fine grain and the soft sheen of photo paper. Ordinary, wholesome, and very wrong. The print is clean: no writing, digits, name plates or stamps.
